correctness.rationale: In the canonical zero-sum Euclidean realization, the polar is the projected product of k six-vertex hexagons. Reconstructed identity ||πf||²=k/2−[t(1−t)E+W²/(2k)] with E split-pair count and W=Σs_i(1−t ε_i) reduces the universal maximum to exact arithmetic. Even k has E=0 and W=0, radius sqrt(2/k). Odd k has only the E=0 cost 1/(2k) or E=1 cost t(1−t)+(1−t)²/(2k); the two t-regime inequalities strictly exclude E>=2. Their crossing is t=(2k−2)/(2k−1). Unsplit centered normals span pair-mean H_{k−1}, while a split contact at any pair and its reversed orientation add all pair-difference coordinates, so center locus has affine dimension k before crossing and 0 at/after crossing. Finite independent exact rational reconstruction enumerated k=2,3,4; for k=3 at t=4/5 it found maximum 4/3 and 30 contacts, in agreement with the union count; at k=3,t=9/10 it found squared norm 169/120 and 24 contacts. This is corroboration, not the all-real-t proof. Endpoint t=0 and t=1 excluded.
